questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the matrix $D$ given below?

- $det(D)=1$
- $D$ is a singular matrix
- $det(D)=0$

 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that a square matrix is singular if its determinant is equal to $0.$

Using the formula, we take the alternating sum of the entries in the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(D) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 7\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(28-30)-2(7-5)+3(6-4) \\  & =1\cdot (-2)-2\cdot 2+3\cdot 2 \\  & =-2-4+6 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $det(D)=0$, the matrix is singular. 

Therefore, only statements II and III are true.

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Determinant of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula, we take the alternating sum of the entries in the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}7 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =7|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}|-3|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =7(6-1)-1(0+3)-3(0+9) \\  & =7\cdot 5-1\cdot 3-3\cdot 9 \\  & =35-3-27 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the matrix $M$ given below?

- $det(M)=10$
- $det(M)=-5$
- $M$ is a singular matrix

 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 3 & 5 \\ -3\sqrt{5} & 3 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that a square matrix is singular if its determinant is equal to $0.$

Using the formula, we take the alternating sum of the entries in the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 3 & 5 \\ -3\sqrt{5} & 3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =\sqrt{5}|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ -3\sqrt{5} & 4\end{aligned}|+\frac{1}{3}|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -3\sqrt{5} & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =\sqrt{5}(12-15)-0+\frac{1}{3}(0+9\sqrt{5}) \\  & =\sqrt{5}\cdot (-3)+\frac{1}{3}\cdot 9\sqrt{5} \\  & =-3\sqrt{5}+3\sqrt{5} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $det(M)=0$, the matrix is singular. 

Therefore, only statement III is true.

choices.value: None of the given statements are true

questions.worked_solution:
Let's use our formula to find an expression for the determinant in terms of $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(B) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & k+2 & -5 \\ 4 & -1 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =3|\begin{aligned}k+2 & -5 \\ -1 & 6\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}1 & k+2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(6\cdot (k+2)-(-5)(-1))+2(1\cdot (-1)-4\cdot (k+2)) \\  & =3(6k+12-5)+2(-1-4k-8) \\  & =3(6k+7)+2(-4k-9) \\  & =18k+21-8k-18 \\  & =10k+3\end{aligned}
$$

Since the determinant of the matrix is $70,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}10k+3 & =70 \\ 10k & =67 \\ k & =\frac{67}{10}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Find, in **ascending order**, the values ​​of $x$ for which the following matrix is singular.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}x+2 & 2x & 4 \\ 3 & x & x+1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

In ascending order, $x=$
{{field-1}} and $x=$
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's use our formula to find an expression for the determinant in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}x+2 & 2x & 4 \\ 3 & x & x+1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & =(x+2)|\begin{aligned}x & x+1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|-2x|\begin{aligned}3 & x+1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|+4|\begin{aligned}3 & x \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(x+2)(3x)-2x(8-x)+4(-x) \\  & =3x(x+2)-2x(8-x)-4x \\  & =3{x}^{2}+6x-16x+2{x}^{2}-4x \\  & =5{x}^{2}-14x\end{aligned}
$$

Since the matrix is singular, the determinant is $0,$ and we have
 

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}^{2}-14x & =0 \\ x(5x-14) & =0 \\ x & =0\,\text{or}\,x=\frac{14}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the solutions are $x=0$ and $x=\frac{14}{5}.$
